preconditions.description: The graph has n vertices, m edges (connected), and k clones (1 ≤ k ≤ n).

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= xi <= n and 1 <= yi <= n for xi, yi in edges)
preconditions.description: Each edge connects vertices within the valid range [1, n].
The input contains exactly m edges.

postconditions.description: Exactly k clone routes are output, one per line.
Each clone route must visit at least one vertex (its starting vertex).

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= c <= 6 for c in [len(route) for route in clone_routes])
postconditions.description: Each clone route has at most 6 vertices (as per the first sample's constraint).

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= v <= n for route in clone_routes for v in route)
postconditions.description: All visited vertices are within the valid range [1, n].

postconditions.expression: all(route[0] in route for route in clone_routes)
postconditions.description: Each clone's starting vertex is included in its route.

postconditions.expression: all(any(v == u for route in clone_routes for v in route) for u in range(1, n + 1))
postconditions.description: Every vertex in the graph is visited by at least one clone.

postconditions.expression: all(all(route[i] in {route[i-1], route[i+1]} if 0 < i < len(route) - 1 else True for route in clone_routes for i in range(1, len(route) - 1)))
postconditions.description: Each consecutive pair of vertices in a route must be connected by an edge (or be the same vertex for self-loops).
